title: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

sense.text:
The books written by the white man say it plainly: from the time of Egypt down to our own times the status of this race has been slavery, slaves at all times, in all places, under all forms of government, and they ask who will say that slavery is not their doom. That is Deuteronomy 28 and Jeremiah 2. But slavery is not our doom. Slavery is not our doom forever.

“It is of the Lord’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.” When we ask our people why we were not destroyed in slavery, they give credit to that man on the screen, Martin Luther King Jr., and say if it wasn’t for him we’d be dead as a people. Us being here today and not consumed has nothing to do with Martin Luther King Jr., who integrated us into white society. It is of the Lord’s mercies. We must start to change our speech and give credit where credit is due.

“They are new every morning”: God’s compassions are new every morning. Martin Luther King ain’t here now; the Lord’s compassion was here way before Martin Luther King. That is not saying he was an evil dead spot or anything like that; it is saying we must give credit to the Creator, give credit to God Almighty. “Great is thy faithfulness.”
“The Lord is my portion, saith my soul; therefore will I hope in him.” We got to start to admit that the Lord is our portion, and we got to hope in him. The him is the Lord.

“The Lord is good unto them that wait for him, to the soul that seeketh him. It is good that a man should both hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the Lord.” So we got to wait for the salvation of the Lord.

“It is good for a man that he bear the yoke in his youth.” This is for the young men. The yoke is Christ’s yoke; we all take that yoke, but it is best to take it when you’re young, at a youthful age, before the clock starts ticking and you start going down before you’re about to die. Once you reach 35 you’re at your midlife; once you go 36 you’re going down. That goes for the ladies too: get mad if you want, it is what it is, it’s Bible.

precepts.why: Before getting to Lamentations: “For thus saith the Lord God, the Holy One of Israel; In returning and rest shall ye be saved; in quietness and in confidence shall be your strength”. In quietness and confidence shall be our strength. So throughout all the slavery, God says in quietness and confidence shall be our strength. Slavery is not our doom; we return, we rest, and we quietly wait for the salvation of the Lord.

For you young men out there, even the one with the shades on: “My son, gather instruction from thy youth up”. You young men, gather instruction from your youth up. Don’t wait till you’re 45 and 50 to say, oh, now I’m going to get my life together. Don’t do that. “So shalt thou find wisdom till thine old age.” That is bearing the yoke in your youth.

“If thou hast gathered nothing in thy youth”: brothers, you young men, if you have wasted your life, sat around playing video games, sleeping till 12 noon, you are preparing your lifestyle to be that of a bum. “How canst thou find any thing in thine age?” How are you going to learn anything when you get older? Your mind is stronger when it’s young. Don’t wait till old age: now I want to get a good wife, brother, now I want to get a house. Bro, you almost 60 years old, the hell is this? You ain’t going to do nothing.

This is the yoke of Lamentations 3:27. “Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me”: Christ said take my yoke upon you. We all take that yoke now, but it is best to take it when you’re young, before the clock starts ticking. “For I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.” Christ said his yoke is easy, his burden is light.

sense.text:
Jeremiah wrote the book of Lamentations. To lament is a passionate expression of grief or sorrow; that is what Lamentations means. Reading this book years ago, it was depressing: why is this in the Bible? Jeremiah was going through it, but it reflects our life.

Read from 27 to get the context: “It is good for a man that he bear the yoke in his youth. He sitteth alone and keepeth silence, because he hath borne it upon him.” The it is the yoke. Brothers, never be afraid to be alone. Sometimes being alone is good: alone time is study time, time to recollect, time to get your life together. You don’t always need a woman in your face 24/7.

“He putteth his mouth in the dust”: why? Because of that yoke you are catching hell. Just like Job, just as we are, we catch hell at times. We bear that yoke, we try to get our lives together, and we are going to go through hard times at one point or another. “If so be there may be hope”: hope to come up out of that low state.
“He giveth his cheek to him that smiteth him: he is filled full with reproach.” Just like Christ; Christ is in this verse. Just as Christ, so was Jeremiah, so are we.

precepts.why: “Wherefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes.” So when we go back to Lamentations 3:29, he putteth his mouth in the dust because, just like Job, just as we are, we catch hell at times. We bear that yoke, and we go through hard times.

Christ in Lamentations 3:30: “I gave my back to the smiters, and my cheeks to them that plucked off the hair”. He gave his cheek to him that smote him. Some people ask how we know Christ had a beard; this is the verse you go to to prove Christ had a beard. So just as Christ was filled full with reproach, so was Jeremiah, so are we.

sense.text: “For the Lord will not cast off for ever”: the Lord will not cast his people off forever. Right now the thought is that God has cast us off forever. He will not cast us off forever, irregardless of what people say, irregardless of what the church system has set up and lied about. We are down in the dust right now, in a low state, but there is a rising up again.
“But though he cause grief, yet will he have compassion according to the multitude of his mercies.” Yet will he have compassion on who? The Israelites.
“For he doth not afflict willingly nor grieve the children of men.” He does not afflict us willingly nor grieve us.

“To crush under his feet all the prisoners of the earth”: the Lord doesn’t want to crush us all under his feet on the earth. We are the prisoners on this earth, that’s us. That is what was read earlier in those books, that our status always seems to be slavery, and it is Bible based.
“To turn aside the right of a man before the face of the most High”: he doesn’t want our right to be turned aside.

“To subvert a man in his cause, the Lord approveth not.” So now, as prisoners on this earth, we are being crushed, our rights are being turned aside, and we are being subverted in our cause, and the Lord approves not.

precepts.why: Paul had to address that dumb thought, that God got rid of the Israelites. “I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid.” The answer is no. “For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin. God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew.” Foreknew means from the past, from the time of Genesis. He has not cast us away. We are down in the dust right now, in a low state, but there is a rising up again.

For you doubters out there: “Thus saith the Lord, which giveth the sun for a light by day, and the ordinances of the moon and of the stars for a light by night, which divideth the sea when the waves thereof roar; The Lord of hosts is his name”. Then “If those ordinances depart from before me, saith the Lord, then the seed of Israel also shall cease from being a nation before me for ever.” If the ordinances of the sun, the moon and the stars depart, then Israel ceases; they have not, so the Lord has not cast us off forever. That’s why when you get up you got to look up and see that sun, moon and stars and say thank you Jesus, thank you Lord.

Yet will he have compassion according to the multitude of his mercies: “He will turn again, he will have compassion upon us; he will subdue our iniquities; and thou wilt cast all their sins into the depths of the sea.” So remember that stuff you used to do, smoking weed, adultery, child molestation: the Lord says he is going to take all that and cast it into the sea. You got to start your lives anew.

What does it really mean that he does not afflict us willingly nor grieve the children of men? “Say unto them, As I live, saith the Lord God, I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked”. That wicked there is us, doing wickedly. “But that the wicked turn from his way and live”: the Lord wants the wicked among us to turn and live. “Turn ye, turn ye from your evil ways”. So all you hoes out there, turn from your evil ways; all you homos out there, turn from your evil ways; all you child molesters out there, turn from your evil ways; all you thieves and liars out there, turn from your evil ways. “For why will ye die”: you got an opportunity, why will you die? “O house of Israel”: that’s the proof he is talking to us.

We are the prisoners on this earth. What was read earlier in those books, that our status always seems to be slavery, is Bible based: “Is Israel a servant? is he a homeborn slave? why is he spoiled?” Are the Israelites servants? Anytime you open the Bible, the twelve tribes of Israel are in captivity. It’s like, what the hell is going on here with this people? And here we are today, thousands of years later, still in that same captivity.

This helps explain how we are crushed, our rights turned aside and subverted in our cause. “Therefore the law is slacked”: because we are in captivity, God’s law is slacked. “And judgment doth never go forth”: true judgment never goes forth. “For the wicked doth compass about the righteous; therefore wrong judgment proceedeth.” As a result wrong judgment proceeds. The wicked there are all the other nations; it started with the Babylonians, and now we are in Babylon the great, the same metaphor.

The next precept. “Therefore is judgment far from us”: we’re the prisoners of the earth; we want judgment but we’re not getting true judgment. “Neither doth justice overtake us”: we want true justice but justice does not overtake us. “We wait for light, but behold obscurity”: we wait for truth but behold confusion. “For brightness, but we walk in darkness.”

“We grope for the wall like the blind, and we grope as if we had no eyes.” Every man and every woman here and watching has eyes, so what does it mean? We are looking for help in all the wrong places. We see injustice but we make believe we don’t see it. You didn’t just see that there was no justice for Tamir Rice? The wall in this case is the church: we’re in the Baptist Church walking along around the walls, I didn’t see what I just saw, pastor give me a good message of motivation, help me. Or we go to the Democrats or the Republicans: help me, I don’t understand. Like you didn’t just see that.

“We stumble at noonday as in the night”: it’s sunshine out here and we are still stumbling; you see the rock right there and you stumble over it. That’s like people who raise their children to tell everybody I love you. Years ago, working security at a store, a little kid came up: I love you, you love me. I said I don’t love you, get the hell away from me, and told the mother, you don’t know if I’m a pedophile or what, and you right there ain’t paying attention, I’m doing you a favor. Don’t have your kids saying I love you to strangers; that’s just stupid, and then your kid disappears and you don’t know what happened. You’re a stupid parent.

“We are in desolate places as dead men. We roar all like bears”: we roar out there in the streets crying because so and so got killed, so and so got ran over or imprisoned for injustice. “And mourn sore like doves”: that’s the women, some of the women mourn like doves. “We look for judgment, but there is none”: there is no proper judgment for our people. And that’s for you reparation seekers out there too. Money is not bad, but you are spending your whole life fighting for reparations, and you ain’t getting it; it ain’t going to work. “For salvation, but it is far off from us.”

Here’s the reason: “For our transgressions are multiplied before thee, and our sins testify against us”. This is why there is no protest that’s ever going to succeed led by women; check history, there is no successful revolution led by women and homosexuals. Women are the greatest supporters of homosexuality; they always want that gay friend, he’s my friend, we share beauty secrets. Sister, he wants your man; you’re just stupid. “For our transgressions are with us; and as for our iniquities, we know them”: that’s why people get mad at the brothers on the street teaching. They’re mad because they know you’re right; they know that Bible you’re reading is right.

“In transgressing and lying against the Lord, and departing away from our God, speaking oppression and revolt”: speaking oppression and revolt is speaking religion and politics. Both of them are an oppressive system and both of them teach you to revolt against God’s laws, both those institutions. “Conceiving and uttering from the heart words of falsehood”: thinking of a lie and uttering words of false lies.

“And judgment is turned away backward”: this is why we get no justice from this white man. God is saying, because you revolt against me, I’m going to have your enemies revolt against you. So we sing we shall overcome and hold that sign, I am a man, no justice no peace. Hell no. The Lord said because you revolt against me, I’ll have your enemies revolt against you; you ain’t going to get no justice, you ain’t going to get no true judgment here in captivity. God raised him up as a weapon to punish us. Now they are the weapon, but when the time comes God is going to turn it around and turn us into the weapon.

“And justice standeth afar off”: we want justice here, but justice is way back there; you run toward justice and justice is going far away from you. “For truth is fallen in the street, and equity cannot enter. Yea, truth faileth; and he that departeth from evil maketh himself a prey”: if you repent you make yourself a prey. “And the Lord saw it, and it displeased him that there was no judgment.”

sense.text:
We are “the prisoners of the earth.” The Lord has us crushed under feet in this captivity, and here are examples of it: our men and women sitting in prison for four decades and more, many of them old men and women now, who went in in their twenties and are in their seventies today.

The Guardian put it out plainly: ‘Black power behind bars’, the black radicals still in prison after four decades, Black Panthers, Black Liberation Army members and the MOVE organization out of Philadelphia, where they dropped C4 on the place they lived and burnt the whole block up. When you go down that list it says they are incarcerated for the murder of a police officer. Those are the same police in the seventies who were doing evil against us, shooting us in the street and beating us in the streets. The murder they are talking about is called self-defense.

With MOVE, one of them had a gun and shot a cop while the cops were shooting at the building, and they charged all of them with it, a lot of them who didn’t even know what was going on. Why didn’t they do that over January 6, when those Edomite cops got killed? They do it with black people. That is the injustice they do in the law.

Most people could care less about our people incarcerated, don’t give a damn. But the little rights we got right now are because of these people that are still incarcerated. And the women are in it too: black women who are political prisoners of the police state, one who was railroaded for standing against police brutality, and one sister that brothers broke out of prison and got on a plane to escape to Cuba, where she lives on asylum. They called her armed and dangerous, and they always try to disrespect our people when they change their names; they want to keep that slave name on you.

“To turn aside the right of a man before the face of the most High.” Our rights as men are being turned aside before the face of the Most High, and he sees all of it.

That sister in Cuba said it: ‘people get used to anything’; the less you think about your oppression, the more your tolerance for it grows, until people think oppression is the normal state of things, and to become free you have to be acutely aware of being a slave. ‘Never let your enemies choose your enemies for you.’ ‘No one is going to give you the education you need to overthrow them.’ That is why the white man will never tell you that we are the Jews, or that Jesus is black. Nobody is going to teach you your true history and your true heroes if they know that knowledge will help set you free. That is a rare woman, a revolutionary-thinking woman; brothers, if y’all going to get married, find a woman like that. These men and women are incarcerated or on the run because they were trying to keep their sons and daughters from dying at the hands of white supremacy.

“To subvert a man in his cause, the Lord approveth not.” Our cause has been subverted, and the Lord does not approve of it, but he allows it. He allows it because of the oppression and revolt that we speak against him (Isaiah 59). We revolt against him, so he lets our enemies revolt against us.

One of our sons who died under the hands of white supremacy told his mother, by text, the names of the people who would do it if something happened to him, and his mother is still trying to find out what happened. Nobody talks about it but us. That is what Isaiah 59 and Lamentations 3 are talking about. Then the names go on and on: George Floyd, Tamir Rice, and more and more. There are so many that we can’t even call their names off the top of our heads. That is a cause subverted, and there is no true judgment for our people here in captivity.

It is like the movie Queen and Slim: a racist Edomite cop pulls the two of them over looking for a reason to arrest the brother, she is a lawyer and tells him what he is doing is breaking the law, he pulls his gun to shoot her, the brother jumps him, the gun goes off and the cop dies, and now they’re on the run. The brother was defending himself and her. That is what these men in prison were doing.
“Who is he that saith, and it cometh to pass, when the Lord commandeth it not?” That’s these preachers. They say a thing and say it will come to pass, when the Lord never commanded it.

“Out of the mouth of the most High proceedeth not evil and good?” Preachers don’t understand that the Bible talks about evil and good. God does evil in this earth and he does good. A Christian will never preach that; they’ll say the devil made me do it. But God controls the devil. God controls Satan and his army and his minions.

precepts.why:
“Behold, the prophets say unto them, Ye shall not see the sword, neither shall ye have famine; but I will give you assured peace in this place.” That is what many of the religious leaders say today. Many of these Christian preachers say 2024 is the year of prosperity, you will become rich this year, and guess who’s in the church: single black women, ‘this is my year, girls.’ Are you kidding me? You’re not going to get rich this year. You might get hit by a car.

“The prophets prophesy lies in my name: I sent them not, neither have I commanded them, neither spake unto them.” God said I sent them not. “They prophesy unto you a false vision and divination, and a thing of nought, and the deceit of their heart.” And the end of them: “By sword and famine shall those prophets be consumed.”

These are the same men today, the gospel singers and the big preachers, the ones that say America will go on forever, God bless America, God loves everybody, prosperity, make that money. One of them puts on the African garb to fool any black person that starts to wake up and feel a little conscious, and then brings him right back to white Jesus. They say it will come to pass, and the Lord never commanded it: that is Lamentations 3:37.

“I form the light, and create darkness.” God said he forms the light, and he creates darkness on this earth. “I make peace, and create evil.” He makes peace on this earth, and he creates evil on this earth. “I the Lord do all these things.”

This is the evil and good that proceeds out of the mouth of the Most High. A Christian will never preach that; they’ll say the devil made me do it. God controls the devil, and Satan and his army and his minions.

“Shall a trumpet be blown in the city, and the people not be afraid?” Just like in times of war, men stood on a tower with trumpets to warn the people of oncoming war and disaster as they saw it. What God is talking about today are the prophets: the prophets blow the horn, they preach the Bible about destruction coming.

“Shall there be evil in a city, and the Lord hath not done it?” There is no evil in a city that the Lord has not done.

“Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.” He won’t do anything but he reveals his secrets, in the Bible, unto his servants the prophets. The prophets must prophesy, and that’s when the evil begins. That is how it works: evil and good both proceed out of the mouth of the Most High.

sense.text:
“Wherefore doth a living man complain, a man for the punishment of his sins?” What you complaining about, brother? Sister, what you complaining about? You’re complaining because you’re being punished for your sins. You kept your legs open every day of the week for Tom, Dick and Harry, now you caught an STD and you mad at God: why God do this to me? Close your legs. And now a brother is willing to take you with your STD, and you tell him you can’t marry him because he’s a little overweight? Sit down somewhere, get married and heal.

So many times we complain about our sins. But when you come in the truth and you know you’re being judged for something you did, you have to deal with it. You have to endure it.

precepts.why:
“I will bear the indignation of the Lord.” That is when you come in and you realize you’re being punished for what you done did. “Because I have sinned against him.” You don’t complain; you bear it.

“Until he plead my cause, and execute judgment for me.” We bear it until the Lord pleads our cause and executes judgment for us, the cause that has been subverted in this captivity. “He will bring me forth to the light, and I shall behold his righteousness.”

sense.text:
We’re talking about complaining for your sins. “Beloved, think it not strange concerning the fiery trial which is to try you, as though some strange thing happened unto you.” The fiery trial deals with a lot of things. Ultimately, write this down, it is talking about tribulation, but there are things that happen when you come into this truth to build your spirit up.

It is to try you. You will be tried in this truth, and ultimately the trial will be tribulation. Some of us will lose our homes, our houses, our lives, our spouses; some of us will be incarcerated. So the point is, like we just read in Lamentations, what are you complaining for? You act like this is something strange, like it’s unheard of.

“But rejoice, inasmuch as ye are partakers of Christ’s sufferings.” The Bible says rejoice in your sufferings, because you are partakers of Christ’s sufferings. That’s the tribulation. “That, when his glory shall be revealed, ye may be glad also with exceeding joy”: when Christ’s glory is revealed, we’re going to be just like him. That’s power.

Here’s the point right there. “If ye be reproached for the name of Christ, happy are ye”: if you brothers and sisters are reproached for the name of Christ, you should be happy, “for the spirit of glory and of God resteth upon you.” Being reproached for the name of Christ proves the holy spirit is on you. The brothers that almost got ran over in Colorado: the spirit of Christ was upon them.

“On their part he is evil spoken of”: on the world’s part Christ is evil spoken of, “but on your part he is glorified.”

“But let none of you suffer as a murderer.” Don’t let none of you brothers or sisters suffer as a murderer, and don’t say you’re being persecuted for Christ if you’re a murderer. We are supposed to suffer for Christ’s name, not for murder because you were trying to rob somebody. You murdering your people for a dollar fifteen, and now you in jail talking about I’m being persecuted for righteousness’ sake? That’s a lie. God’s law says thou shalt not kill.

“Or as a thief, or as an evildoer.” The man in the first video was a thief and a murderer; the man in the second was a thief and an evildoer, and evildoer can cover a lot of things. He stood in front of the judge saying he was in a better place and not committing crimes now, and then he was over that bench. Sisters, these are questions a lot of you don’t ask men: some men are suffering a mental health crisis and are on meds or need to be on meds. Women keep finding the same guy attractive, knowing he was no good to the last woman, and have a baby by him anyway because he’s cute, he’s six-two, broad shoulders, she can change him. And it don’t matter how good-looking a woman is, she could be a thief too.

“Or as a busybody in other men’s matters.” These are the gossip shows and busybody videos, the ones that run up millions of views in two days. Brothers, we might laugh at this stuff, but we cannot be caught up in it, which is gossip. We are the prophets of the Lord and ambassadors of Christ, and we must act like it.

One lie can destroy a lot of people. A fifteen-year-old sister in 1987 said she had been raped by white men, police among them, and was found in a trash bag with racial slurs written on her body; it was almost a race riot, black people and black leaders stood behind her, her advisers took it to national prominence, and then a grand jury found it was a lie. The prosecutor she accused sued her and her advisers for defamation and won, and one of the lawyers lost his license to practice law. One lie destroyed a lot of people’s careers. That’s why, brothers, when I say don’t get involved in gossip, don’t do it: if somebody decides to sue for what you said, all hell is going to break loose, and they’re not going to sue Joe Schmo.

precepts.why:
“My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.” When you come in this truth, prepare your soul for temptation. Your life might have been good, but when you come in this truth the Lord is going to show you that what you thought was good, you just accepted as normal. It was never good.

You might have thought you had a good marriage. A brother said up here, I thought I had a good marriage until we came into this truth, then I realized my wife was the head of the house. That’s not a good marriage; it was an oppressive marriage he had accepted as normal. When he started to change it, stop bossing me around, stop telling me what to do, this is how we’re going to do it, all hell broke loose in the house. That is the fiery trial which is to try you: think it not strange.

“No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life.” Brothers, we are at war; this is war. So if we are at war we cannot entangle ourselves with the affairs of this life, and all that gossip and who is a power bottom is the affairs of this life. Some of it might be funny and amusing, but you men are the prophets of the Lord. We’ve got to leave that stuff alone. Don’t do videos on it, because you might suffer for it, and that is suffering as a busybody in other men’s matters, not for the name of Christ.

Y’all see what one little lie can do: it can destroy. “Curse the whisperer and doubletongued: for such have destroyed many that were at peace.” “A backbiting tongue hath disquieted many, and driven them from nation to nation: strong cities hath it pulled down, and overthrown the houses of great men.” That is what a backbiting tongue, gossip, a lie, can do.

“A backbiting tongue hath cast out virtuous women, and deprived them of their labours. Whoso hearkeneth unto it shall never find rest, and never dwell quietly.” Don’t listen to lies, don’t listen to gossip; that is what God is telling us, avoid it.

“The stroke of the whip maketh marks in the flesh: but the stroke of the tongue breaketh the bones.” When people say sticks and stones may break my bones but words can never hurt me, that’s a lie. Words can hurt you; words can break bones. “Many have fallen by the edge of the sword: but not so many as have fallen by the tongue.” People telling lies against people have gotten many people killed and put out of their homes and houses.

That gossip YouTuber who was sued for millions for slander and lost the case is the proof of it, and now another celebrity is suing her. Y’all think them videos is funny, but when you run around repeating that stuff you will get in trouble behind it, and God ain’t with you: Lord, why am I in trouble? Because you didn’t obey what I told you. Let others gossip; we should not be involved in gossip. Stay in the scriptures, don’t add to what an article says and don’t take away from it, and don’t take it personal when somebody talks crap about us. It’s bigger than you.

Christ said unto the Pharisees, “Ye are they which justify yourselves before men; but God knoweth your hearts: for that which is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of God.”

Bring that up to today: many of our people esteem Hollywood stars and entertainers, and Christ said that which is highly esteemed among men is abomination. Anybody that is esteemed in this society, Christ is letting us know, has committed abomination; there are things they have done behind the scenes to get where they are. So whether the gossip about some big preacher is true or not, we don’t know and don’t give a dag on; it has nothing to do with us. We stick with what the Bible says, not with being a busybody in other men’s matters.

sense.text: “Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to the Lord.” Let us search and try our ways means what? Examine ourselves. That is self-examination: taking a moral compass on yourself, like taking an aptitude test. Every man and every woman must examine themselves and find the pitfalls in their own life, because we can only find out what you allow us to see, or what God reveals in the body. Then “turn again to the Lord.”

“Let us lift up our heart with our hands unto God in the heavens.” Stop teaching your kids to pray with their hands closed. That ain’t what the Bible ever says. Lift up your hands when you pray to the Lord; don’t put your hands together and hide them. Stop teaching your kids to lie.

“Thou hast covered thyself with a cloud, that our prayer should not pass through.” It feels at times when we pray to the Lord that he ain’t listening, because we’re not getting the result that we want when we pray. The Lord is saying, hold on, it ain’t yet the time.
“Thou hast made us as the offscouring and refuse in the midst of the people.” That’s what Paul said: the offscouring, like dung, the doodoo of the earth. It was true back then and it’s true today.

“All our enemies have opened their mouths against us.” All our enemies speak against God’s truth. They think they’re speaking against us, but it’s really against God; it’s against what his law says, his words. Watch how the enemies speak against us: they accuse us day and night, they say they are not guilty for what they did to us because we are in the midst of sin, and they search out our iniquities and push sin on us through the entertainment world.

It reaches into everything. Harvard University’s black female president was put out and replaced. In the hearing in Congress they tried to say she was for murdering Jewish students; she spoke very eloquently. They asked her how far freedom of speech goes and she said it depends; they asked her if it was okay to murder Jews and she said of course not. When they couldn’t get her on that, they came up with a plagiarism accusation and took her out of that position. Not just that: they speak against the prophets too, us.

precepts.why:
“Let us search and try our ways” means self-examination, and Paul says it plainly: “Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves. Know ye not your own selves”.

So the Bible says examine yourselves, and by examining yourselves you have to find your strengths and your weaknesses. What are the pitfalls in your life? Every man and every woman must examine themselves, because the body can only find out what you allow us to see, or what God reveals. That self-examination is how we turn again to the Lord.

Read with “Let us lift up our heart with our hands unto God in the heavens.” “Now no chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous, but grievous: nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby.” The chastening we are under is grievous now, but afterward it yields the peaceable fruit of righteousness.

“Wherefore lift up the hands”: lift up your hands when you pray to the Lord. Don’t put your hands together and hide them; stop teaching your kids to pray with their hands closed, that ain’t what the Bible ever says, and stop teaching your kids to lie. “Lift up the hands which hang down, and the feeble knees”.

“And make straight paths for your feet”: make your life straight, “lest that which is lame be turned out of the way”. That which is lame is your sins. You have to self-identify what is sin in your life, which goes back to searching and trying our ways.

“Thou hast made us as the offscouring and refuse in the midst of the people”: that’s what Paul said. “Being defamed, we intreat: we are made as the filth of the world, and are the offscouring of all things unto this day.” Being defamed as the Israelites. The Israelites are made as the filth of the world, the offscouring, like dung, the doodoo of the earth, of all things unto this day. It was true back then and it’s true today.

This goes with verse 46, “All our enemies have opened their mouths against us.” “And I heard a loud voice saying in heaven, Now is come salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of his Christ: for the accuser of our brethren is cast down”, which accuses them “before our God day and night.”

They accuse us day and night: you are not the Israelites, you’re not the Jews the Bible speaks of, you’re African-Americans, you’re Puerto Ricans, you’re Dominicans. That is how the enemies open their mouths against us, first and foremost.

“All that found them have devoured them”: all that found us devoured us in slavery. “And their adversaries said, We offend not, because they have sinned against the Lord, the habitation of justice, even the Lord, the hope of their fathers.”

See what our enemies say: what they do to us, they’re not guilty, because we’re in the midst of sin. That is how they open their mouths against us.

This is what the heathens said about the Israelites, the 12 tribes. “If there be any error” means sin in this people, “and they sin against their God, let us consider that this shall be their ruin”: this is their ruin as a people. “And let us go up, and we shall overcome them”: we can easily defeat the Israelites if they’re in the midst of sin.

“But if there be no iniquity in their nation”, if they have repented of their sins, “let my lord now pass by”: leave the Israelites alone, “lest their Lord defend them”, “and we become a reproach before all the world”, a reproach like doodoo on the planet. The enemy speaks against us and comes against us because of our sin, the same as Jeremiah 50:7.

This is more of how the enemy speaks against us. “They search out iniquities; they accomplish a diligent search: both the inward thought of every one of them, and the heart, is deep.”

They search out iniquities: movies, film, music, the entertainment world. They know it influences everybody throughout the earth, including our people.

We are not a sinless people. We do have sin, but it’s exacerbated, because we watch and listen to things that promote sin. “Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners.” Evil communications are the things you watch, the things you listen to, the people you hang around. They corrupt good manners: they corrupt God’s laws.

The examples are all over social media: a woman saying she’s sexually liberated and a goddess. They gassed her up: queen, you’re the goddess of the earth, now open your legs. Another one catches a disease and says somebody took advantage of her in a moment of weakness. Brothers, they lie. Did he rape you? No. She saw him, he was cute, handsome, she thought he had it all together.

He wasn’t crap, and guess who wasn’t crap either: she wasn’t crap either. He’s a piece of doodoo and she’s a big piece of doodoo too. That’s how it is, and it’s Bible; God said it, it wasn’t made up. “A wicked woman is given as a portion to a wicked man”: two pieces of doodoo collide. You’re a misogynist, you hate women? No; I just don’t kiss women’s behind.

We’re glad brothers and sisters are in here trying to get their lives right, but there’s always that one, she or he, waiting: who can I burn, who can I take advantage of. There are people in here that ain’t no good, looking to burn you.

sense.text: Not only do they speak against our people; they speak against the prophets too. “Fear and a snare is come upon us, desolation and destruction.” Brothers and sisters, just as it was back then, it’s going to happen again to the prophets in Tribulation.

“Mine eye runneth down with rivers of water for the destruction of the daughter of my people.” There’s going to come a day when we’re going to cry. “Mine eye trickleth down, and ceaseth not, without any intermission”: with no stopping of the crying for the destruction of the daughter of our people.

“Till the Lord look down, and behold from heaven.” We must wait until the Lord intervenes.

Go back to verse 44 with it: “Thou hast covered thyself with a cloud, that our prayer should not pass through.” We’re going to be praying to the Lord for help and assistance, and the Lord ain’t going to help us until verse 50, “till the Lord look down, and behold from heaven.” We got to wait on his good kindness for him to intervene. He’s not going to move when we want him to move.

“They have cut off my life in the dungeon, and cast a stone upon me.” The dungeon is jail, brothers. There may even come a time when they send certain brothers to Guantanamo Bay, never to be heard of again. They call them political prisoners: you don’t get a lawyer there, nobody represents you, there’s no trial. Some of you don’t know what I’m talking about; look it up.

When it says they have cut off my life in the dungeon and cast a stone upon me, it means you ain’t never getting out; you’re going to die in there. That’s what Jeremiah prophesied about what happened during the time of Babylon, and that’s what he’s also prophesying about during these turbulent times.
“Waters flowed over mine head; then I said, I am cut off. I called upon thy name, O Lord, out of the low dungeon.” Again, that low dungeon is prison, jail, Guantanamo even.

“Thou drewest near in the day that I called upon thee”: the day that we call upon the Lord, he will draw near. Then hear the Lord’s response: “thou saidst, Fear not.” Those two words, fear not. That’s the same thing Christ said in Revelation chapter 2: don’t fear what you must suffer, be thou faithful unto death. It’s the same thing.

“Thou hast seen all their vengeance and all their imaginations against me.” The nations imagine mischief against the prophets, just like they did during the time of Jeremiah. David prophesied about it.

“Thou hast heard their reproach, O Lord, and all their imaginations against me; The lips of those that rose up against me, and their device against me all the day.” Jeremiah is saying the same thing David prophesied about, the same thing we just read in the Psalms.

“Behold their sitting down, and their rising up; I am their musick.” I am their music, meaning we are their discussion. They may have code words for us, but we are always their discussion.

When they sit down, when they lay down, and when they rise up in the morning, they’re talking about the Israelites, about our people: how can we keep them in sin, and not only that, how can we make a profit off of it, exploit them.

Listen good to what Jeremiah says in prayer: “Render unto them a recompence, O Lord, according to the work of their hands.” A recompense is a judgment: do to them according to the evil that they have done to us, Lord.
“Give them sorrow of heart, thy curse unto them.” God cursed them. You’re never going to read this in church.

“Persecute and destroy them in anger from under the heavens of the Lord.” You’re never going to hear this in church, you’re never going to hear this in Sunday school, but that’s what the Bible says to say. Meanwhile there’s a grimy Christian on TV swagging and surfing on so-called New Year’s Eve. That ain’t Jesus.

precepts.why:
The dungeon is jail, and Christ speaks of it. “I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty, (but thou art rich) and I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan.” The synagogue of Satan are those that call themselves Jews, but they’re not. Christ said that’s blasphemy: just to call them Jews is blasphemy.

“Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer”: notice what Christ says, don’t fear what you must suffer. “Behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison.” The devil shall cast some of you: that’s why we don’t say everybody’s going to prison, but the devil will lock some of us in prison. That’s what God says prophetically.

“That ye may be tried”: to be tried means tested. The Lord’s going to try our faith, test our faith. You say you believe? Go through this. “And ye shall have tribulation ten days”: tribulation means you’re going to catch hell for ten days.

“Be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life.” He says, but listen, I want you to be faithful unto death. A crown of life means eternal, everlasting life. That means world dominion, power like you’ve never seen before, that celestial body.

“He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; He that overcometh shall not be hurt of the second death”: he that overcomes will not be hurt of the Lake of Fire. That is the hope for the brothers cut off in the dungeon of Lamentations 3:53, and it is the same fear not the Lord answers with in verse 57.

David prophesied about the nations imagining against us: “The wicked plotteth against the just, and gnasheth upon him with his teeth.” The wicked plot against the just. They speak against us, and that’s called propaganda: ‘oh they are guilty of the Jersey shooting, they kill people in a store, oh they want to kill everybody.’ That’s what these so-called, what they call Zionists say, and they ain’t Zion at all.

“Hide me from the secret counsel of the wicked”: hide me from the secret counsel of the nations, of the white man. “From the insurrection of the workers of iniquity.”

This is an insurrection of the wicked. They sit down and gather together in meetings that we are not invited into, and the discussion many times, especially in these think tanks, is the Israelites: what are we going to do today against the Israelites. That is all their imaginations against me in Lamentations 3:60-62.

“I am their musick” in Lamentations 3:63 is Job’s “And now am I their song”: their discussion. We are always their discussion.

When the class came back to it after reading the rest of the chapter: and now they’re talking about us, now we’re no damn good. They make songs about us. They tell black men and black women, I want you to make a song about how … ain’t …, how the women are …; I give you a whole lot of money, and that’s what they do. “Yea, I am their byword.”

Jump up to verse 1: “But now they that are younger than I have me in derision”. They that are younger than I: we are God’s heir, we are his chosen; they’re not. (Exodus 4:22 and 1 Chronicles 16:13 prove it.) “Whose fathers I would have disdained to have set with the dogs of my flock”: Job said, I would not have allowed it, I would have hated for them to sit with the dogs of my flock.

“For want and famine they were solitary”: for want, for lack, and famine. “Fleeing into the wilderness in former time desolate and waste”: this is what it’s talking about, the Caucasus mountains of Georgia, Russia. “They were driven forth from among men”: you see the history. “They cried after them”: we cried after the white man like he stole something. Our ancestors chased him and ran him up to the Caucasus mountains of Georgia, Russia.

“To dwell in the clifts of the valleys, in caves of the earth, and in the rocks.” This is what the Bible is prophesying about; this is where your caveman dwelt at. We didn’t live there; that’s where the white man lived at. “Under the nettles they were gathered together.”

“They were children of fools, yea, children of base men”. Base is the root word of basement: it’s the bottom, you can’t get no lower than them. That’s what God says: they are the basest of men. And you want to have a baby with him? A rapper just had a sperm donor from an Edomite. “They were viler than the earth”: God said they were viler than the earth. And now am I their song: these are the ones that make us their music.

Here’s the proof of what younger than I means in Job 30:1: “Thus saith the Lord, Israel is my son, even my firstborn”. Israel is the firstborn, God’s heir. They are the younger, and they have us in derision.

This is what it means, they that are younger than I. “O ye seed of Israel”: that’s us, you and I. We are his servants. “Ye children of Jacob, his chosen ones”: we are the children of Jacob, we are the chosen ones of the Lord, not them.

Let’s see what Jesus said about praying for vengeance. “He spake a parable unto them to this end, that men ought always to pray”: we got to always pray, brothers and sisters. Pray in the evening, pray in the morning, and pray at noontime.

“There was in a city a judge, which feared not God, neither regarded man”: this judge represents the Lord. “And there was a widow in that city”: the widow represents the Israelites; that’s proven. “And she came unto him, saying, Avenge me of mine adversary.” This widow, the Israelites, said avenge me of my adversaries, my enemies. That is Jeremiah’s prayer in Lamentations 3:64, “Render unto them a recompence, O Lord”.

“And he would not for a while”: the Lord did not for a while. Hold that, and go back to Lamentations 3:44: “Thou hast covered thyself with a cloud, that our prayer should not pass through”, meaning the Lord wasn’t listening.

Then, “but afterward”. Go back to Lamentations 3:50: “Till the Lord look down, and behold from heaven.” Now read the whole verse: “And he would not for a while: but afterward he said within himself, Though I fear not God, nor regard man; Yet because this widow troubleth me, I will avenge her, lest by her continual coming she weary me.” The Lord holds back for a while, then he looks down from heaven and avenges, because we keep coming to him.

“And the Lord said, Hear what the unjust judge saith.” Here’s the breakdown, verse 7, in case you think I don’t know what I’m talking about: “And shall not God avenge his own elect, which cry day and night unto him, though he bear long with them?” Which cry, which pray day and night unto him. “I tell you that he will avenge them speedily”: Christ said he will avenge you speedily.

“Nevertheless when the Son of man cometh, shall he find faith on the earth?” Will you be praying for that thing, or will you have given up hope? ‘I’ve been praying for vengeance, Lord ain’t doing nothing.’ The Lord been working: earthquakes in Japan left and right. Y’all don’t see the Lord at work? He smoked Libya and Morocco, one with a flood and one with an earthquake. And you see what’s happening to the Palestinians in Gaza. The Lord ain’t done yet; he’s just getting started, because everybody got to pay for what they did to the 12 tribes of Israel. Everybody going to get it. The Lord got plenty to go around.

sense.text:
The first half of the class was about our people, because our people don’t like to hear about our people; we want to hear prophecy. I gave you something to think about about yourselves first, to examine yourselves. Now we talk about some prophecy.

“Concerning Edom, thus saith the Lord of hosts; Is wisdom no more in Teman? is counsel perished from the prudent? is their wisdom vanished?” Teman during the Middle Ages was the Ottoman Turks. Why is it saying this about Teman? Teman was known for counsel and wisdom; they were the wise.

Operation Paperclip shows it. It was a secret United States intelligence program in which more than 1,600 German scientists, engineers and technicians were taken from the former Nazi Germany to the United States for government employment after the end of World War II, between 1945 and 1959. But I thought America was against the Nazis? No, they weren’t. They gave them jobs, and they didn’t take just any old Germans: they took the smartest, the most intellectual ones, the scientists and the engineers. Many of these Germans were former members, and some were former leaders, of the Nazi party. They forgave them everything, wiped their record clean and said, you come work for us. There was nobody screaming anti-Semitism, no ADL saying get all of them out. They were complicit with it too. This ain’t gossip; y’all can find documentaries on this.

The picture of a former V2 rocket scientist who became a NASA director, sitting between US President John F Kennedy and US vice president Lyndon B Johnson at a 1962 briefing at Cape Canaveral: they got receipts that these Nazi scientists were brought here to work for America. America took all the best of Teman and brought them to the United States of America.

precepts.why:
“Shall I not in that day, saith the Lord, even destroy the wise men out of Edom”: he’s going to destroy the wise men out of Edom, “and understanding out of the mount of Esau”. “And thy mighty men, O Teman, shall be dismayed, to the end that every one of the mount of Esau may be cut off by slaughter.” Teman is the wisdom of Edom, and that wisdom is what the Lord destroys.

Put up a map of modern-day Teman: the Lord’s not talking about this right here. The West Bank is controlled by the Arabs; just Arabs, not the Palestinians but the Arabs. Write that down. That’s how we know it ain’t talking about this yet: Esau is on the left side, over there where it says Israel. That’s where they’re at currently; they’re trying to move their way in, but not yet.

On the modern-day map you see Jordan, where the Arabs are; the West Bank, which the Arabs have control of; so-called Israel, where the Ashkenazi are; and the Gaza Strip, where the Palestinians are being blown up currently. Israel is moving into the West Bank; they haven’t finally blown that place up yet, but that’s what’s going on. Y’all need to be able to look at a map once in a while and know what you’re looking at.

Oppenheimer: his father was from Nazi Germany, and he went to college in Germany. ‘Now I am become death, the destroyer of worlds’, the line he took from the Hindu scripture, the Bhagavad Gita. He was the father of the atomic bomb (the atom bomb; nuclear came later). I’m showing you the wisdom in Teman.

“Behold, I have created the smith that bloweth the coals in the fire”: the smith, or the scientist, that bloweth the coals in the fire, “and that bringeth forth an instrument for his work; and I have created the waster to destroy”. That’s these ICBM nuclear weapons today. America took all the best of Teman, and they brought them to the United States of America.

“For thou hast said in thine heart, I will ascend into heaven”: I will create the first airplane. “I will exalt my throne above the stars of God”: that’s space travel; that’s when he landed on the moon.

“I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north”: put a picture of slavery up. How many of y’all saw the movie Mandingo? They used to put their feet on us to draw out the rheumatism. That’s how they would sit on us; just some of the cruel things they would do, and these are little boys, not grown burly-back men. Isaiah 14 is heavy; it’s deep, there’s a lot up in there.

“I will ascend above the heights of the clouds”: it’s talking about planes. That’s the beginning, in 1903, the Wright Brothers; write that down. From that point in history they created greater, expanded technology: modern airplanes. “I will be like the most High.”

With Isaiah 14:13, “I will exalt my throne above the stars of God”: “Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle, and though thou set thy nest among the stars”. Back to the moon: when he landed on the moon in 1969, brothers, what did they say? ‘The eagle has landed.’

I’m still showing you they took the best of Teman and brought them to the United States of America to expand their technological advancements. “Behold, thou art wiser than Daniel”: see what it says about Esau. “There is no secret that they can hide from thee”.

“With thy wisdom and with thine understanding thou hast gotten thee riches”: with their wisdom and understanding they have gotten the riches. The Industrial Revolution, the age of invention: discoveries and inventions, the factories, the railroads. Henry Ford; they say he made the first automobile. The creation of the first computer, and what it expanded into. Wall Street: this is how they got riches. The slaves were the first commodity, and it went from there.

“And hast gotten gold and silver into thy treasures”: the laptops; the television (when I was young we had a big box with maybe five channels, and it ended at 12 midnight); 5G, when everybody was running around crazy about it, and now everybody got 5G. All the technological advancements: they have gotten the riches, gold and silver into their treasures.

“By thy great wisdom and by thy traffick hast thou increased thy riches, and thine heart is lifted up because of thy riches”. “Therefore thus saith the Lord God; Because thou hast set thine heart as the heart of God; Behold, therefore I will bring strangers upon thee, the terrible of the nations”. Hear what God said: he’s going to bring the terrible of the nations upon them.

I’m showing you their wisdom. “I considered the horns, and, behold, there came up among them another little horn”: the little horn is America. “Before whom there were three of the first horns plucked up by the roots”: write this down. That’s the French American war, where they plucked up the French; the Spanish American war, where they plucked up the Spanish; and the war of independence, where they plucked up the British.

“And, behold, in this horn were eyes like the eyes of man”, meaning they saw great inventions; they had vision like no other nation on earth had. That is the wisdom of Teman. “And a mouth speaking great things”: their communication system, their media system, speak great things, like evolution, the Big Bang theory, and Jesus is white.

“And of the ten horns that were in his head, and of the other which came up, and before whom three fell; even of that horn that had eyes, and a mouth that spake very great things”: that horn we just read about, “whose look was more stout than his fellows.” That part right there means America became greater than all nations on earth. Put up the military: America’s everywhere. They are bigger and greater than any nation you can mention, bigger and greater than Russia, Germany, Canada, China, Japan, Africa, with technology like nobody’s business. That’s what the Bible’s talking about.

sense.text:
“Flee ye, turn back, dwell deep, O inhabitants of Dedan”: Dedan is the Arabs. Dedan was one of Abraham’s children by Keturah, so the Arabs are not of Ishmael. Get that straight: they are from Keturah, not Hagar.

“For I will bring the calamity of Esau upon him, the time that I will visit him.” The Arabs are not getting away. The same calamity that comes upon Esau is going to come upon Dedan. That is what God is saying in verse 8.

God is saying about Esau, “If grapegatherers come to thee, would they not leave some gleaning grapes?” You go through a field hungry and you take some grapes, but you leave some. “If thieves by night, they will destroy till they have enough.” A regular thief leaves something behind, but not Esau. Esau takes everything.

“But I have made Esau bare, I have uncovered his secret places.” His secret places are the underground bunkers where they meet, decked out with carpet, with water and boats under there, behind doors you ain’t getting through. They don’t let the average negro go up in there; there’s not one negro in there. Think God loves everybody? Tell them to let you up in their bunkers and see what happens: you are going to meet God.

“And he shall not be able to hide himself: his seed is spoiled”: his descendants are spoiled, “and his brethren, and his neighbours, and he is not.” He is not going to be any more. That is thus saith the Lord.
“Leave thy fatherless children, I will preserve them alive; and let thy widows trust in me.” Verses 11 and 12 are talking about Israel. God is not telling Esau to trust in him.

“For thus saith the Lord; Behold, they whose judgment was not to drink of the cup have assuredly drunken”: this is how you know that part is talking about us. We were not supposed to drink of the cup of judgment, because we were God’s chosen; we just read that in Chronicles. But we have surely drunk the dregs of the cup of judgment, which is Deuteronomy 28.

Then he says to Esau: “and art thou he that shall altogether go unpunished?” Should you go unpunished? “Thou shalt not go unpunished, but thou shalt surely drink of it.” You are going to drink too.

“For I have sworn by myself, saith the Lord, that Bozrah shall become a desolation”: desolation means uninhabitable; nobody is ever going to live there. “A reproach, a waste, and a curse; and all the cities thereof shall be perpetual wastes.”

“I have heard a rumour from the Lord, and an ambassador is sent unto the heathen, saying, Gather ye together, and come against her, and rise up to the battle.” Notice in verse 15 what God says about Esau: “For, lo, I will make thee small among the heathen, and despised among men.”

America supports Israel. Look at the map: so-called Israel is small, and they follow Judaism, Zionism. All around them, Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Lebanon, are Muslims, a lot of them Arabs, some of them Esau. Israel is small among them and nobody likes them, nobody, and because of America’s support they don’t like America either.
“Thy terribleness hath deceived thee.” This is a terrible people; this is what they do to nations. Look at what they are doing in Gaza.

precepts.why: Who is Dedan? “And Jokshan begat Sheba, and Dedan.” See Dedan right there. Put Jeremiah 49:8, Isaiah 21:13 and Genesis 25:3 next to each other in your notes: that is how you take good notes.

Jump up to verse 1: “Then again Abraham took a wife, and her name was Keturah.” Keturah bare him Jokshan, and Jokshan begat Dedan, so Dedan was one of Abraham’s children by Keturah. The Arabs come from Keturah, not from Hagar; they are not of Ishmael.

“The burden upon Arabia. In the forest in Arabia shall ye lodge, O ye travelling companies of Dedanim.” Dedanim, that’s Dedan right there, in the burden upon Arabia. So the inhabitants of Dedan in Jeremiah 49:8 are the Arabs, and the calamity of Esau is coming upon them too.

He shall not be able to hide himself. “And the kings of the earth, and the great men, and the rich men, and the chief captains, and the mighty men, and every bondman, and every free man, hid themselves in the dens and in the rocks of the mountains.” These are their secret places, the bunkers in the dens and in the rocks, and God has uncovered them.

“And it shall be, if they refuse to take the cup at thine hand to drink, then shalt thou say unto them, Thus saith the Lord of hosts; Ye shall certainly drink.” God told Jeremiah to take this cup to all the nations, and the cup is a metaphor. He did not literally walk around saying, hey Moab, drink this. He went with prophecies and said you are going to drink this cup, meaning they are going to suffer the consequences. It is like when Christ said, are you able to drink of the cup that I shall drink of? He was not talking about a literal cup; it was symbolic of what was about to happen.

“For, lo, I begin to bring evil on the city which is called by my name, and should ye be utterly unpunished?” The city called by God’s name is Jerusalem. “Ye shall not be unpunished: for I will call for a sword upon all the inhabitants of the earth, saith the Lord of hosts.” Judgment began with us, but everybody is going to drink of it.

To prove that verse 11 is talking about Israel and not telling Esau to trust in God: “Because I delivered the poor that cried, and the fatherless, and him that had none to help him. The blessing of him that was ready to perish came upon me: and I caused the widow’s heart to sing for joy.” The fatherless and the widows God preserves are Israel.

Here’s another precept. “Rejoice and be glad, O daughter of Edom, that dwellest in the land of Uz; the cup also shall pass through unto thee”: the Edomite is going to drink the same cup we had to drink. “Thou shalt be drunken, and shalt make thyself naked.”

“The punishment of thine iniquity is accomplished, O daughter of Zion”: there is going to come a day when our judgment is accomplished, finished. When Christ comes back, it’s over, brothers and sisters. “He will no more carry thee away into captivity”: we will never go into slavery ever again. “He will visit thine iniquity, O daughter of Edom; he will discover thy sins.”

Here’s the precept for Bozrah. “For my sword shall be bathed in heaven: behold, it shall come down upon Idumea, and upon the people of my curse, to judgment. The sword of the Lord is filled with blood, it is made fat with fatness, and with the blood of lambs and goats, with the fat of the kidneys of rams: for the Lord hath a sacrifice in Bozrah, and a great slaughter in the land of Idumea.” Bozrah is Edom’s, and the sword of the Lord comes down there in a great slaughter.

An example of their terribleness. “He who smote the people in wrath with a continual stroke”: they don’t let up, they don’t stop. “He that ruled the nations in anger”: in love, in harmony, in democracy, in anger. “Is persecuted”: persecution is coming upon them. “And none hindereth.”

“They that see thee shall narrowly look upon thee, and consider thee, saying, Is this the man that made the earth to tremble, that did shake kingdoms”: how do they make the earth tremble and shake kingdoms? With bombs, devastation. “That made the world as a wilderness, and destroyed the cities thereof.” This is what the Bible is prophesying about: that is their terribleness. The house of his prisoners is the prisons we read about earlier in Lamentations.

sense.text:
“Thy terribleness hath deceived thee, and the pride of thine heart, O thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, that holdest the height of the hill.” To understand this you got to know a little bit of history. Brothers that teach, in New York and in all the various camps, must know the difference with the clefts of the rock. Esau has always loved to dwell in the clefts of the rock, but when the clefts of the rock come up in the beginning, in Genesis, it is not the Caucasus mountains. That is the Middle Ages. During Genesis they lived at Mount Seir: Genesis 36, that is where they dwelt, the area God gave them.

“Though thou shouldest make thy nest as high as the eagle, I will bring thee down from thence, saith the Lord.” The symbol is the eagle, the one on the dollar bill, and that is talking about America first and foremost. When they landed on the moon, the flight of Apollo 11, July 20th 1969, they said ‘the eagle has landed’. They became famous for being known as the eagle. They made their nest as high as the eagle, and God says he will bring them down from there.
“Also Edom shall be a desolation.” Edom shall be a desolation, starting with America. “Every one that goeth by it shall be astonished, and shall hiss at all the plagues thereof.”

“As in the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah.” How was Sodom and Gomorrah overthrown? Fire and destruction. That is how God says America is going down. “No man shall abide there, neither shall a son of man dwell in it”: nobody is going to live here ever, ever again.

“Behold, he shall come up like a lion”: America shall come up like a lion, “from the swelling of Jordan”, over there in Israel. On the modern map that is Jordan today, and America is going to come right to that area to fight; the whole fight is going to be in that area, especially Israel. Don’t leave Israel out.

“Against the habitation of the strong”: the strong are these Arabs, the Arabs and the Iranians coming against Israel. “But I will suddenly make him run away from her”: God is going to suddenly make America run away.

“Therefore hear the counsel of the Lord”: hear the Bible, the counsel “he hath taken against Edom”, against Esau, “and his purposes, that he hath purposed against the inhabitants of Teman.”

“Surely the least of the flock shall draw them out.” Israel is the least of the flock, the modern day Israelis. The least of the flock shall draw America out, “surely he shall make their habitations desolate with them.”

“The earth is moved at the noise of their fall, at the cry the noise thereof was heard in the Red sea.” Everybody is going to hear about the fall of America, because America is so prideful she thinks she can never be taken down. The noise is going to be heard in the Red Sea.

“Behold, he shall come up and fly as the eagle.” Here he goes back to explain what he is talking about: the jets. When the Arabs and the Iranians come against Israel, when those nations come, America is coming. America coming to the rescue, America coming to save the day: ‘there’s no need to fear, America is here.’ That is what they are doing.

He shall “spread his wings over Bozrah: and at that day shall the heart of the mighty men of Edom be as the heart of a woman” in her pangs. What does that mean is going to happen to America? She is going to be destroyed.

“Because of the wrath of the Lord it shall not be inhabited”: America shall not be inhabited. “But it shall be wholly desolate”: this place shall be wholly desolate. “Every one that goeth by Babylon shall be astonished, and hiss at all her plagues.” The same words Jeremiah uses for Edom in 49:17, the astonishment and the hissing at all the plagues, are used here for Babylon.

So this is not talking about ancient Babylon, the Babylon in the time of Nebuchadnezzar, which is modern day Iraq. Do people live in Iraq today? They do. So it is not talking about that; it is talking about the United States of America. Edom and this Babylon are one: the desolation of Edom starts with America.

“Where the nations of the dragons of Arabia shall come out with many chariots, and the multitude of them shall be carried as the wind upon earth, that all they which hear them may fear and tremble.” The dragons of Arabia are the Arabs.

“Also the Carmanians”: the Carmanians are the Iranians. They go forth raging in wrath “as the wild boars of the wood, and with great power shall they come, and join battle with them, and shall waste a portion of the land of the Assyrians.” The land of the Assyrians is modern Israel today; they are going to waste a portion of it.

“And then shall the dragons have the upper hand, remembering their nature”: the dragons, the Arabs of verse 29, shall have the upper hand, “conspiring together in great power to persecute them”, in great power to persecute Israel.

That is the habitation of the strong in Jeremiah 49:19: the Arabs and the Iranians coming against Israel. That is when America comes up like a lion from the swelling of Jordan, and God suddenly makes him run away; and the least of the flock, Israel, draws America out.

“But I will remove far off from you the northern army.” The Lord is going to remove the northern army, America’s military, far off from us, because we are going to be catching tribulation here.

“And will drive him into a land barren and desolate”: that is talking about over there in Israel, that whole area. “With his face toward the east sea”: the east sea is the Dead Sea, on the right of the map. “And his hinder part toward the utmost sea”: the utmost sea is the Mediterranean, on the far left. So the fight is going to be right there in that area, between the Dead Sea and the Mediterranean.

“And his stink shall come up, and his ill savour shall come up”: destruction upon destruction. That is the fall of Jeremiah 49:21 whose noise the whole earth hears, heard as far as the Red Sea.
